title: What Happens When You Get a Fever?
description:
Most providers call it a fever at 100.4 F (38 C). It happens when your brain's thermostat resets to a higher temperature, mostly in response to an infection, and many people feel chilled when they have one. Shivering makes your muscles contract and relax, and that movement warms your body. Get lots of rest and drink plenty of fluids (water is best). Adults should call a healthcare provider if a fever goes above 103 F (39.4 C) or lasts longer than about three to four days.
